name: Tsunamis
description: Tsunami messages and decisions for local sources (minutes to the first wave) and distant sources (hours): warning, advisory, watch and information statement messages, international threat messages, evacuation timing and cancellation. For warning centers, coastal counties, ports and harbors.
outsideParties: the National Weather Service forecast office (dissemination)
the Coast Guard and the harbor master
county emergency management and the sheriff
the port authority and ferry operators
schools, hospitals and campgrounds in the inundation zone

advisorRoles.name: Tsunami Warning Duty Scientist (advisor)
advisorRoles.description: Explains message levels, arrival times and the evidence behind an upgrade or cancellation.

decisionForms.label: Issue, upgrade or cancel a tsunami message
decisionForms.description: The warning center's message level and areas.

decisionForms.label: Order an evacuation
decisionForms.description: Order the evacuation of a tsunami hazard zone.

decisionForms.label: Port and harbor action
decisionForms.description: Move vessels to deep water, close the port or hold vessels at the dock.

glossary.definition: Highest level: widespread flooding expected, take action now. Can be sent as a Wireless Emergency Alert.
Strong currents and waves dangerous to people in or near the water are expected; stay out of the water and away from beaches and harbors.
A possible tsunami for an area, issued early for a distant event; be ready. Not sent as a Wireless Emergency Alert.
No action needed: an earthquake occurred with no threat expected, or an update.
Deep-ocean pressure buoys and coastal gauges give observed wave heights that confirm or cancel a message.

productConventions: Messages carry a number, issue time with zone, areas, a short evaluation, preliminary earthquake parameters, arrival times and the next update.
Local sources give minutes to first arrival; distant sources give hours. A distant source usually starts as a Watch, then upgrades or cancels as observations arrive.
International threat messages list coasts with threat categories and UTC arrival times.
realismRules: For a nearby source, people should move on feeling long or strong shaking, without waiting for a message. The first message may reach people after the first wave.
Preliminary magnitude changes; do not state wave heights before gauge or buoy observations.
Later waves can be larger than the first. The local all clear belongs to local officials, not the warning center.
A Watch is never sent as a Wireless Emergency Alert.
